name: Uncertainty + cosine-decayed coarse
tagline: Kendall uncertainty weights for fine and coarse, with a piecewise warmup-then-cosine decay that fades the coarse loss to a 0.1 floor.

key_hyperparams.name: warmup_frac
key_hyperparams.role: fraction of epochs with full coarse weight

key_hyperparams.name: floor
key_hyperparams.role: asymptotic coarse weight after cosine decay

diff_from_baseline: Adds a deterministic warmup-plus-cosine curriculum on the coarse term to Kendall uncertainty weighting; coarse-loss precision still learnable but is multiplied by a schedule that decays from 1 to 0.1, unlike vanilla uncertainty (constant) and DWA (relative-rate weighting).

name: Uncertainty + polynomial coarse decay
tagline: Kendall uncertainty weighting with $(1-t)^{\beta}$ decay applied only to the coarse precision and an L2 penalty on the log-variances.

key_hyperparams.name: β
key_hyperparams.role: polynomial decay exponent on coarse weight

init_recovers: Uncertainty weighting at $t=0$ (with extra L2 reg)
diff_from_baseline: Augments Kendall uncertainty with a fixed polynomial decay on the coarse precision (vs. constant) and a quadratic regularizer on log-variances; never re-balances on gradient conflict like PCGrad and ignores DWA's relative-rate signal.

name: EMA-gated coarse valve (RAMTV)
tagline: Detects per-batch task interference via EMA loss ratios, exponentially shuts the coarse 'valve' and re-allocates the freed weight to fine; cosine fade overall.

key_hyperparams.name: momentum
key_hyperparams.role: EMA decay for per-task loss tracking

key_hyperparams.name: weight sum
key_hyperparams.role: conserved total weight reallocated to fine

init_recovers: Equal weights $w_f=w_c=1$ at first batch and $t=0$ with no interference
diff_from_baseline: Replaces uncertainty/DWA's loss-rate or learnable-precision schemes with a per-step EMA-conditioned valve plus a fixed cosine global fade, and conserves total loss mass by routing closed-coarse capacity into the fine task; PCGrad-style gradient surgery is replaced by scalar reweighting only.

name: Coupled coarse with EMA guidance
tagline: Multiplicatively couples the auxiliary coarse term to the fine residual; EMA-normalized residual and curriculum gates an aux weight tied to fine difficulty.
init_recovers: Fine-only at $t=1$ (curriculum→0); near-base aux at $t=0$ when EMA matches init
diff_from_baseline: Unlike Kendall uncertainty (per-task log-variance) and DWA (rate-of-loss-change), this gates the coarse term through a guidance signal $g$ built from EMA-normalized residual losses and explicitly couples it to the current fine loss, so an easy fine batch reduces aux pressure and a hard one raises it.

name: Calibrated coarse + exponential decay
tagline: Rescales coarse loss by the early-training fine/coarse ratio, then applies a fixed exponential schedule decaying coarse weight from 0.7 to 0.08.
init_recovers: Pure fine CE as $t\to\infty$ (coarse weight $\to 0.08$); near 1.0+0.7r at $t=0$
diff_from_baseline: Drops Kendall uncertainty altogether; uses a fixed exponential schedule plus one-shot loss-magnitude calibration instead of learnable precisions or DWA-style rate weighting, and never inspects gradient conflict (no PCGrad).
